title: NaruServe-servlet public surface: ServletAdapter, ServletConfigurer, NaruServeInitializer and the init-parameters
requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-servlet`, package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet`, the public final class `ServletAdapter` implementing `HttpAdapter`, the public `@FunctionalInterface ServletConfigurer` with `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder builder) throws Exception`, and the public `NaruServeInitializer` implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, registered in `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, which reads the context init-parameters `naruserve.configurer` and `naruserve.urlPattern`; the module has no `jakarta.servlet` counterpart in v1.
rationale: Covers D-358, D-363 (container registration and class names), wave decisions Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007), Who builds the app on the Servlet adapter (r4 W2-003) and Servlet SSE registration (r4 W2-005); answers Q-4. Measured (2026-10-20): `NaruServe-servlet/src/main` holds only `package-info.java`; `build.gradle` declares `javax.servlet:javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` and `javax.websocket:javax.websocket-api:1.1` `compileOnly` for the module; a built `RestApp` has no adapter setter and `RestApp.Builder` takes `httpAdapter`, `jsonCodec` and `logger` (`RestApp.java:226-270`). Decision (C-07): the names are `ServletAdapter`, `ServletConfigurer`, `NaruServeInitializer` and the package-private `NaruServeServlet`; the initializer is discovered through the Servlet 3.0 service file, so an application only sets the init-parameter; `naruserve.urlPattern` defaults to `/*` and accepts `/*`, `/` or `/prefix/*`; the servlet is named `naruserve` and registered with `asyncSupported=true` and no `MultipartConfig`. When `naruserve.configurer` is absent the initializer does nothing, because the jar may sit in `WEB-INF/lib` of an application that does not use NaruServe. Pitfall: `@HandlesTypes` is not used, so no classpath scan runs at container start. Rejected alternative: a `ServletContextListener` declared in `web.xml` or by `@WebListener`; it needs the application to list it and `@WebListener` needs annotation scanning, which a jar in `WEB-INF/lib` loses when `metadata-complete=true`.
acceptanceCriteria: Reflection finds `ServletAdapter` public, final, implementing `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.HttpAdapter` with a public no-argument constructor; `ServletConfigurer` a public interface annotated `@FunctionalInterface` whose only abstract method is `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder)` declared `throws Exception`; `NaruServeInitializer` a public class implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`; and package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet` annotated `@NullMarked`. [D-358; D-363]

The built module jar holds `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer` whose only line is `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet.NaruServeInitializer`, read from the jar as `DefaultAppFactoryTest` reads the bootstrap services file. [D-363]

On an embedded Servlet 3.1 container, a web application with the init-parameter `naruserve.configurer` registers exactly one servlet named `naruserve` mapped to `/*`, with `isAsyncSupported() == true` and no multipart configuration; a web application without the init-parameter registers nothing and every request is answered by the container (`404`). [D-363; r4 W2-005]

The init-parameter `naruserve.urlPattern` accepts `/*`, `/` and `/api/*` (mapping the servlet accordingly) and any other value (`api/*`, `*.json`, an empty string) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the parameter and the value. [D-363]

The initializer instantiates the class named by `naruserve.configurer` through its public no-argument constructor and hands it a `RestApp.Builder` that already holds a `ServletAdapter`; a missing class, a class that does not implement `ServletConfigurer`, a class without a public no-argument constructor, a `configure` that throws and a `configure` that returns `null` each make context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the class. [D-359; r4 W2-003]

No class of `NaruServe-servlet` references `jakarta/servlet/` and `settings.gradle` includes no module for `jakarta.servlet`, which the wave 1 class-reference check and `BuildLayoutTest` already assert and wave 8 keeps. [D-358; I-002]

title: Servlet adapter lifecycle: the container initialises the app with onStart and destroys it with shutdown, binds no socket and reports port 0
requirement: The system shall start the app on the Servlet adapter when the container initialises the web application — the initializer installs the `ServletAdapter`, finds the Gson codec by reflection, calls the configurer and then `app.listen(0)`, so `onStart` runs and the state becomes `RUNNING` exactly as on the embedded engine — and shall run `app.shutdown()` when the container destroys the web application; `ServletAdapter.bind` stores the handler and opens no socket, and `boundPort()` and `ServerHandle.port()` are `0`.
rationale: Covers D-359, wave decisions Servlet start path (r2 W2-001), Port on the Servlet adapter (r3 W2-001, which supersedes the first-request port of round 2), Servlet bind (r4 W2-006), Gson on the Servlet adapter (r5 W2-002) and the D-107 bind contract. Measured (2026-10-20): `HttpAdapter.bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` defaults to `bind(host, port, handler)` (`spi/HttpAdapter.java:20-29`); `DefaultRestApp.start` reads `a.boundPort()` once right after bind (`internal/DefaultRestApp.java:506-507`) and `ServerHandle.port()` returns that captured value; `RestApp.Builder.build()` throws `IllegalStateException` without `httpAdapter` or `jsonCodec`; the module `runtimeClasspath` is `NaruServe-api` only (CON-BUILD-006 AC-5). Decision: the destroy callback is a `ServletContextListener` that the initializer adds with `addListener`; a user call of `listen(int)` on an app holding the Servlet adapter takes the same path and binds nothing; `docs/api/servlet.md` tells the reader to take the port from the container. The logger is the one the configurer sets, otherwise the Builder default `ConsoleLogger`, which is also what `RestApp.create()` picks on a JVM without `android.util.Log` (FR-ENGINE-009). Pitfall: because `boundPort()` is read once, a port learned from the first request would never reach `ServerHandle`; round 3 therefore fixed `0`. Pitfall: `Class.forName("com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec")` must use the web application's class loader, not the module's, when the container isolates them. Rejected alternative: a `compileOnly` or `runtimeOnly` dependency on `NaruServe-gson` so the codec is a normal import; it would break the `runtimeClasspath` pin of CON-BUILD-006 AC-5 and I-005.
acceptanceCriteria: On the embedded container, context startup builds the app through the configurer and calls `app.listen(0)` before the first request: `onStart` callbacks have run once, `app.state()` is `RUNNING` and a request is served. [D-359]
Context destruction runs `app.shutdown()`: `onStop` callbacks run, the state is `TERMINATED`, `ServletAdapter.stop` and `release` have been called, and a second destruction is harmless. [D-359]

`ServletAdapter.bind("127.0.0.1", 8080, handler)` and `bind(settings, handler)` return without starting a thread or opening a socket, ignore host and port, and `boundPort()` returns `0` before and after; `ServerHandle.port()` of the app is `0`; a test asserts the adapter alone opens no `ServerSocket` and starts no thread. [D-359; D-107; r3 W2-001]
A user call of `app.listen(8080)` on an app built with a `ServletAdapter` binds nothing, runs `onStart` and reaches `RUNNING` through the same path as the initializer. [D-359; r2 W2-001]

When `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` is on the web application's class path the initializer finds it by reflection and presets it as the codec; the configurer may replace it with `Builder.jsonCodec`; when neither exists startup fails with a `ServletException` whose message contains `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` and `jsonCodec`. The module `runtimeClasspath` stays `NaruServe-api` only. [r5 W2-002; I-005]
A failing `onStart` callback (an `AppStartException` from `listen`) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` that carries it as cause, and no thread of the app remains. [D-359; I-015]

Deviation (recorded): the frozen D-416 thread total of 451 (452 with the keeper thread, PERF-APP-001 AC-2) bounds the embedded TinyHttpd app; on the Servlet adapter the threads are the container's plus at most `maxSseStreams` SSE threads (FR-SVL-005), and `docs/api/servlet.md` says so. [D-416]

title: Servlet request mapping: raw path minus context path and servlet mapping, raw query, headers, and the same application types as on the embedded engine
requirement: The system shall map each servlet request to the `HttpExchange` values the core expects — `methodToken`, the raw `getRequestURI()` with the context path and the url-pattern prefix the initializer registered stripped at a segment boundary and kept percent-encoded, the raw `getQueryString()`, `getProtocol()`, every header value in received order with duplicates kept, `getRemoteAddr()`, `isSecure()` and `getInputStream()` — so that routes, middleware, `Request`, `Response` and `Cookie` behave as on the embedded engine.
rationale: Covers D-360, D-363 (path handling), D-399, D-052, wave decisions Servlet path edge cases (r2 W2-003) and Servlet path and WebSocket answer (r3 W2-004: the remainder is the request URI minus the context path minus the url-pattern prefix, not `getServletPath()`), and I-021. Measured: `HttpExchange.rawPath()` is "the raw request-target path, undecoded" and `httpVersion()` is the request-line version such as `HTTP/1.1` (`spi/HttpExchange.java:27-37`). Decision: context path `/app`, pattern `/api/*` and URI `/app/api/users/%41;v=1` give the path `/users/%41;v=1`; patterns `/*` and `/` strip nothing after the context path; an empty remainder is the path `/`; path parameters (`;name=value`) stay in the path as in Express; when the raw URI does not start with the context path plus the prefix at a segment boundary (the remainder must be empty or start with `/`) the adapter answers `404` with the standard error body through the `ErrorRenderer` of the settings. Pitfall: containers match servlet mappings on the decoded path, so `/app/%61pi/x` can reach the servlet while the raw prefix `/api` does not match; `getServletPath()` and `getPathInfo()` are decoded and normalised and must not be used (D-399). Pitfall: `getParameter*` would consume a form body (FR-SVL-004). Rejected alternative: matching the prefix on the decoded path; it would let an encoded segment change which handler runs.
acceptanceCriteria: With context path `/app` and pattern `/api/*`, a request to `/app/api/users/%41;v=1?x=%20` reaches a route `/users/:id` with `req.rawPath()` equal to `/users/%41;v=1`, `req.param("id")` equal to `A;v=1` and `req.query("x")` equal to a space; with pattern `/*` or `/` the same request without `/api` reaches the same route, and a request to the bare servlet root reaches the route `/` (empty remainder is `/`). [D-363; D-399]

A request whose raw URI does not start with the context path plus the registered prefix at a segment boundary (a test sends `/app/%61pi/users` to pattern `/api/*`) is answered `404` with the standard error body and a request id, and `getServletPath()`, `getPathInfo()` and `getParameter*` are never read, which a recording `HttpServletRequest` proxy asserts. [D-363; r3 W2-004]

Headers reach `req.header(name)` and `req.headers(name)` in received order with repeated names kept, `Cookie` request headers reach the core cookie parser unchanged (`req.cookie("s")` returns a NaruServe `Cookie`, never `javax.servlet.http.Cookie`), `req.remoteAddress()` is `getRemoteAddr()` and `req.isSecure()` is `isSecure()`; `app.trustProxy(true)` takes effect in the core (FR-ENGINE-008). [D-360]

A shared case suite — route parameters, query decoding, JSON body and `res.json`, cookies read and written, `404`, `405` with `Allow`, automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, middleware order, `onError` and the standard error body, `res.file` — runs on the Servlet adapter and on the in-memory adapter with identical statuses and bodies, using the same app definition code, so application code needs no change between engines. [D-360; I-021]

The path-rejection cases of D-052 (malformed percent-encoding, invalid UTF-8, an encoded `/`, an encoded or raw `NUL`, `.` and `..` segments raw and encoded) sent as raw request lines to the embedded container are answered `400`, whether by the container or by the core, and never `2xx`; the `OPTIONS *` request is sent too and its observed status is recorded in `docs/api/servlet.md`. [D-052; I-021]
Header values the framework writes never contain CR or LF on this adapter, and security-related log lines of the adapter carry no token, session id or file content. [I-016; I-017]

title: Servlet response writing: commit, finish, abort, sendFile and a single start per exchange
requirement: The system shall write each response through the container's `HttpServletResponse` — `commit` sets the status with `setStatus` and adds each header in the given order without `sendError`, never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`, and returns the container's output stream; `finish` completes the response; `abort` marks the exchange aborted so that every later write, `commit` or `finish` throws `IOException`; `sendFile` writes exactly `length` bytes of the file from `offset` in bounded chunks; and a second start of the same exchange throws `IllegalStateException`.
rationale: Covers D-360 (the `Response` behaviour is the core's; the adapter must not alter it), wave decision Servlet adapter semantics left open (r2 W2-006: `abort()` marks the exchange aborted and later writes throw `IOException` because the container owns the socket; response header order is the container's) and the SPI contract of `HttpExchange.commit`, `abort` (idempotent, thread-safe) and `sendFile`. Measured: `spi/HttpExchange.java:55-75` states that the adapter never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`, that header chars are at most U+00FF and never CR or LF, and that `abort()` may run on any thread while another thread is writing. Decision: header values are written with `addHeader` as given; the status is set with `setStatus` so the container renders no error page; `abort` does not close the container's socket (the container owns it) and does not call `sendError`; `sendFile` uses `java.io` only (no `java.nio.file`, CON-HTTP-002) and a buffer of at most 64 KiB. Pitfall: `HttpServletResponse.setContentLength` and containers that compute a length for small bodies can change `Content-Length`; the core's header is passed through `setHeader`, and a HEAD response keeps the length the GET body would have had (FR-HTTP-017). Rejected alternative: closing the connection from `abort` through container-specific APIs; it is not portable across containers.
acceptanceCriteria: A handler's `res.status(201).header("X-A", "1").send("ok")` reaches the client as status `201`, header `X-A: 1` and body `ok` with the `Content-Length` the core set; a response with unknown length (`res.stream`) arrives chunked on HTTP/1.1; and no error page of the container appears for a `404` or `500` the core produced, because `sendError` is never called. [D-360]
A HEAD request to a GET route returns the `Content-Length` of the GET body and no body bytes, and a `204` and a `304` carry no body, on the embedded container. [D-360; FR-HTTP-017]

After `abort()` (called from another thread while a body write is in progress) the write fails with `IOException`, a later `commit` and `finish` throw `IOException`, and `abort()` called twice is harmless; a second `commit`, `sendFile` or `eventStream` on one exchange throws `IllegalStateException`. [r2 W2-006]

`res.file` and `res.download` on a file serve the whole file, a single `Range` (`206` with `Content-Range`) and a `416`, byte for byte equal to the in-memory adapter, with `sendFile` copying in chunks of at most 64 KiB and never reading the file into memory; the class references no `java.nio.file` type. [D-360; FR-STATIC-010]
Response header order on the wire is the container's, `docs/api/servlet.md` says so, and no test of the shared case suite depends on header order. [r2 W2-006]

title: Servlet multipart and form bodies go through the core parser over the request input stream
requirement: The system shall serve multipart and urlencoded request bodies on the Servlet adapter through the core parser reading `requestBody()`, the container's input stream, and shall never call `getParts()`, `getPart(...)`, `getParameter*`, or register the servlet with a `MultipartConfig`, so the `app.multipart`, `formLimit` and JSON limits and the body limit of the core apply as on the embedded engine.
rationale: Covers D-363 (multipart support) and wave decision Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007: multipart uses the core parser over the request input stream, not the Servlet `Part` API; the body limit and the JSON limit still apply in the core), r4 W2-005 (no multipart configuration) and I-015. Measured: `internal/MultipartParser.java` is the engine-free parser shared by every adapter (FR-MULTIPART-001). Pitfall: on a POST with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `getParameter*` makes the container read and consume the body, leaving the core an empty stream; the adapter must not touch it. Pitfall: a servlet registered with a `MultipartConfig` makes some containers parse multipart before the servlet and write temp files the core cannot clean. Rejected alternative: `getParts()` with `MultipartConfig` limits; it would duplicate the limits (container versus `app.multipart`) and break the one-parser rule of FR-MULTIPART-001.
acceptanceCriteria: On the embedded container, a multipart request with two files and a text field returns the same `req.file`, `req.files`, `req.form` and `req.parts` values as on the in-memory adapter, and a urlencoded form returns its fields, using the shared case suite of FR-SVL-002. [D-363; FR-MULTIPART-003]

A recording `HttpServletRequest` proxy shows that during these requests the adapter reads `getInputStream()` and never calls `getParts`, `getPart`, `getParameter`, `getParameterMap`, `getParameterNames` or `getParameterValues`, and the registered servlet has no multipart configuration. [r1 W2-007; r4 W2-005]

A multipart body above `app.multipart` file size, part count or total limit is answered `413`, a body above the app body limit is answered `413` and a JSON body above `jsonLimit` is answered `413`, each with the standard error body, and after the response no upload temporary file of the app remains in `tempDirectory`. [D-363; FR-MULTIPART-002; I-015]

A client that closes the connection in the middle of a multipart upload leaves no upload temporary file after the request ends (T17 on this adapter), which a test asserts by listing `tempDirectory` after the container's request thread returned. [FR-MULTIPART-006; I-015]

title: Servlet SSE under AsyncContext: bounded stream counter, dedicated executor and no async timeout
requirement: The system shall implement `HttpExchange.eventStream` on the Servlet adapter so that the exchange counts open streams against `maxSseStreams` (default 128) and answers `503` before the exchange is marked started when the bound is reached, otherwise calls `startAsync()` and `AsyncContext.setTimeout(0)`, commits status and headers, hands the container's output stream to `StreamDrain.attach`, runs the core drain loop on a dedicated bounded executor owned by the adapter — daemon threads named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>`, at most `maxSseStreams`, never the container's pool threads — returns at once so the container's request thread is released after the handler returned, and completes the `AsyncContext` when the drain ends.
rationale: Covers D-361, D-106 (the event-stream point), wave decisions SSE bound and thread owner on the Servlet adapter (r3 W2-002) and Servlet SSE registration (r4 W2-005: `asyncSupported=true` and `AsyncContext.setTimeout(0)` per stream), and I-012 and I-015. Measured: `spi/StreamDrain.java` is the core-owned drain loop type with `attach(OutputStream)`; FR-SSE-003 fixes the TinyHttpd mirror (counter that throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started, drain on the request worker). Decision: the Servlet counter is the adapter's own, with the same `maxSseStreams` of the frozen `ServerSettings`; the executor is created at `bind(ServerSettings, handler)`; heartbeat and event writes are flushed after each write so the container does not buffer them. Frozen: D-106 says the adapter chooses the thread that runs the loop ("an `AsyncContext` on the Servlet adapter"). Deviation (recorded): the loop runs on an adapter-owned executor thread, not on the container's request thread; a container pool thread blocked for the life of a stream would exhaust the pool, and the 128-thread bound keeps I-012 (no unbounded default). Deviation (recorded, inherited from FR-SSE-002 for D-406): sends made inside the handler before the drain starts are written directly on the handler thread, synchronised on the exchange, as on TinyHttpd. Pitfall: the default async timeout of a container (30 s on Jetty 9.4) would end a long stream with a `500`, hence `setTimeout(0)`. Pitfall: checking the counter after the exchange is marked started leaves the dispatcher unable to commit the `503` (r3 W2-001 of wave 7). Rejected alternative: running the drain on the container thread with a blocking loop; it holds one container thread per stream.
acceptanceCriteria: With `maxSseStreams(2)` and two open streams, a third request whose handler calls `res.sse()` receives `503` with the standard error body and its request id, because the adapter's counter throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started; after one stream ends a new `res.sse()` is accepted, and the counter is released also when the drain fails with `IOException` and when the exchange is aborted. [D-361; r3 W2-002]

The drain runs on a thread named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>` that is a daemon and not a container pool thread, the container request thread has returned from `service()` while the stream is open (a test records both thread ids and the return), and the executor never holds more than `maxSseStreams` threads. [D-361; D-106]

The servlet is registered with `asyncSupported=true`, every stream calls `AsyncContext.setTimeout(0)`, and a stream kept open longer than the container's default async timeout (the test lowers it to 1 s) still receives a heartbeat after 2.5 s and is not ended by the container. [r4 W2-005]

An event sent from another thread after the handler returned reaches the client within 500 ms of the `send`, a `: ping` heartbeat reaches an idle client within `heartbeatInterval` plus 500 ms, and an event sent by the handler thread before the drain starts reaches the client while the handler still runs, each flushed without further writes behind it. [D-361; D-406; FR-SSE-002]

When the drain ends (client close, `close()` or the core's end report) `AsyncContext.complete()` is called, the stream's `onClose` listeners run once, and `abort()` on an SSE exchange also calls `AsyncContext.complete()`. [D-361; r5 W2-001]

A stream whose client closed its socket is detected by the next write or heartbeat failing with `IOException`, ends with the access-log cause `client` and returns its executor thread within two heartbeat intervals plus 1 s. [D-361; FR-SSE-004]

title: Servlet stop and release: refuse new requests, wait for in-flight exchanges to the deadline, then cut the rest
requirement: The system shall implement `HttpAdapter.stop(timeout, unit)` on the Servlet adapter so that it first refuses new requests with `503` and `Connection: close`, then waits for the in-flight exchanges until the deadline, and at the deadline calls `shutdownNow()` on the SSE executor and `AsyncContext.complete()` on every stream still open; and `release()` detaches the handler, so that after shutdown no `naruserve-servlet-sse-*` thread and no upload temporary file of the app remains.
rationale: Covers D-359 (shutdown on container destroy), D-107 (two-call stop), wave decisions Servlet stop (r3 W2-003) and Blocked writes of a Servlet SSE stream (r5 W2-001), and I-012, I-015. Measured: the core shutdown sequence runs the before-wait participants (the SSE and WebSocket closing participants, FR-SSE-005) and then `adapter.stop(left(deadline))` (`internal/DefaultRestApp.java:617-619`, FR-APP-011). Deviation (recorded under I-012): a drain thread stuck in a socket write to a client that stopped reading is bounded only by the container's own write timeout, which the adapter does not control; the "cut at timeout" promise of `docs/api/sse.md` therefore holds on the Servlet adapter up to that container bound, and the release documentation lists the deviation (OPS-REL-007). Decision: the adapter counts in-flight `service()` calls and open streams under one lock and waits on its condition; refusing by `503` happens before the core handler runs, using the `ErrorRenderer` of the settings. Pitfall: `stop` called from the container's destroy callback may run on a container thread, so it must not wait for container-owned work beyond the deadline. Rejected alternative: interrupting container request threads at the deadline; interrupting a thread the container owns is unsafe.
acceptanceCriteria: With one slow plain request in flight, `stop(2, SECONDS)` makes a new request answer `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body at once, returns as soon as the slow request finishes (before the deadline), and a request that outlasts the deadline does not make `stop` return later than the deadline plus 1 s. [D-359; r3 W2-003]

With open SSE streams, `shutdown` delivers the closing notice of FR-SSE-005 through the core, each stream's client sees the end of the chunked body within the shutdown timeout plus the D-344 margin, the `AsyncContext` of each stream is completed, and the executor is shut down. [D-359; FR-SSE-005]

A stream whose client stopped reading is cut at the deadline: `stop` returns within the deadline plus 1 s and the stream's `AsyncContext` is completed, while the blocked drain thread may stay blocked until the container's write timeout, which the test does not wait for; the deviation sentence is present in `docs/api/servlet.md` and `docs/api/sse.md` gains a pointer to it. [r5 W2-001]

`release()` detaches the handler (later requests are answered `503`), `stop` and `release` are idempotent, `stop` before `bind` is harmless, and after `shutdown` returns a test finds no thread named `naruserve-servlet-sse-*` alive within 2 s and no upload temporary file of the app. [D-107; I-015]
Every test of the module that starts the container asserts after shutdown that no server thread and no temporary upload file of that app remains (a shared test rule). [I-015]

title: WebSocket is not supported on the Servlet adapter: an upgrade request answers 501, other requests keep 426
requirement: The system shall answer a real WebSocket upgrade request to a route registered with `app.ws` on the Servlet adapter with status `501` and the standard JSON error body, because `ServletExchange.webSocket` (and `upgrade`) throw `HttpException(501)` instead of the SPI default that leads to `500`, while a request without an upgrade to a path that has only an `app.ws` route keeps the core's `426`.
rationale: Covers D-363 (WebSocket support) and wave decisions Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007: Servlet 3.1 has no WebSocket API, so a route registered with `app.ws` answers `501` with the standard JSON error body and `docs/api/servlet.md` says it is not supported in v1) and Servlet path and WebSocket answer (r3 W2-004: `HttpException(501)` because the SPI default would lead to `500`; this applies only to real upgrade requests). Measured: `HttpExchange.webSocket` defaults to throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` (`spi/HttpExchange.java:99-101`), which the core maps to `500`; the core checks Origin before the upgrade extension point (FR-WS-003) and answers `426` for a non-upgrade request before any adapter call (FR-WS-004). Deviation (recorded, for D-408 over TinyHttpd): TinyHttpd replaces `Connection: Upgrade` on a non-`101` response (FR-WS-004 AC-2); on the Servlet adapter the headers pass through `addHeader` to the container, so the test records whether `Connection: Upgrade` reaches the client and asserts `426` and `Upgrade: websocket` only. Rejected alternative: bridging to `javax.websocket` (it is `compileOnly` in the module); the Servlet adapter would then depend on a container-specific endpoint registration and WebSocket stays a v1 non-goal here.
acceptanceCriteria: A request with `Upgrade: websocket`, `Connection: Upgrade`, `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` and a valid key to a path with an `app.ws` route, on the embedded container, receives `501` with the standard error body (a `code`, a `message` and the request id), never `101` and never `500`, and no WebSocket session or upgraded connection is registered. [D-363; r3 W2-004]

A request without `Upgrade` to the same path receives `426` with `Upgrade: websocket`, a request with a rejected `Origin` receives the core's `403` before any `501`, and a request to the same path with a method other than GET keeps its core answer. [FR-WS-003; FR-WS-004]

`ServletExchange.upgrade(headers, handler)` also throws `HttpException(501)`; a unit test calls both methods on an exchange and asserts the status of the exception and that the exchange stays unstarted, so a later `commit` still works. [D-363]

`docs/api/servlet.md` states that WebSocket is not supported on the Servlet adapter in v1, that `app.ws` routes answer `501` there and that the embedded engine serves them, which a docs test asserts. [D-363]

title: Servlet adapter keeps maxSseStreams and the error renderer from the settings and ignores the embedded-engine server options
requirement: The system shall override `HttpAdapter.bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` on the Servlet adapter to keep the frozen settings it uses — `maxSseStreams` and the `ErrorRenderer` (and logger) — while `bind(host, port, handler)` only stores the handler, and shall ignore every `ServerOptions` setting that configures the embedded engine (`allowedHosts`, worker and connection limits, timeouts, header size and bind address and port), listed as ignored in `docs/api/servlet.md`, while the body limit, the JSON limit and the multipart limits still apply in the core.
rationale: Covers D-359, D-363, wave decisions Servlet adapter semantics left open (r2 W2-006) and Servlet bind (r4 W2-006). Measured (2026-10-20): `allowedHosts` is enforced only by the TinyHttpd adapter (`NaruServe-tinyhttpd/.../TinyHttpdAdapter.java:118-120`) and nowhere in `NaruServe-api/src/main` outside `ServerOptions` itself; `bindAddress` and `port` are read only by the TinyHttpd adapter's bind (`:100`); `ServerSettings` carries `maxSseStreams` (default 128), `logger` and `errorRenderer` (`spi/ServerSettings.java:32-56`). Decision: the ignored list in `servlet.md` names `allowedHosts`, `bindAddress`, `maxWorkers`, connection and wait-queue limits, `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `maxHeaderSize`, `maxHeaderCount`, `maxUpgradedConnections` and the WebSocket options; the applied list names the body limit, `jsonLimit`, `formLimit`, `app.multipart`, `maxSseStreams`, the SSE options and `trustProxy`. Pitfall: because `allowedHosts` is an adapter setting, a Host allowlist the application relies on is not enforced behind a container; `servlet.md` tells the reader to configure virtual hosts in the container. Rejected alternative: enforcing `allowedHosts` in the Servlet adapter; the container owns the connector and virtual host, and a second enforcement would diverge from it.
acceptanceCriteria: Reflection finds that `ServletAdapter` declares its own `bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)`, and a test shows that the adapter used `maxSseStreams(3)` (a fourth stream is refused, FR-SVL-005) and the settings' `ErrorRenderer` (a custom renderer's body appears in the adapter's own `503` and `404` answers). [r4 W2-006; D-363]

A test sets `allowedHosts("example.test")`, `bindAddress("10.255.255.1")`, `maxWorkers(1)` and a tiny `maxHeaderSize` on the app and shows the Servlet adapter serves a request with another `Host` header and a normal header block unchanged, so these settings have no effect there. [r2 W2-006]
The body limit still applies: a body above `app.bodyLimit` answers `413`, the JSON limit answers `413` and the multipart limits apply, on the embedded container. [D-363; r1 W2-007]

`docs/api/servlet.md` lists the ignored and the applied settings by name as above, and a docs test checks that each listed name exists on `ServerOptions` or `RestApp` (so the list cannot drift to a name that no longer exists). [D-363]

title: Build placement of NaruServe-servlet: javax.servlet 3.1 compileOnly, embedded container in test scope only, no jakarta module, API 21 modules servlet-free, SPI unchanged
requirement: The build shall keep `NaruServe-servlet` JVM-only with `javax.servlet:javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` and `javax.websocket:javax.websocket-api:1.1` `compileOnly` and a `runtimeClasspath` of `NaruServe-api` only, shall add the embedded javax Servlet 3.1 container `org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-servlet:9.4.58.v20250814` and the Gson module to `testImplementation` of that module only, shall contain no `jakarta.servlet` module in v1, shall keep the seven API 21 modules free of `javax.servlet`, and shall change no `spi` signature.
rationale: Covers D-358, D-362, I-001, I-002, I-004, I-005, I-006, I-014 and wave decision Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007). Measured (2026-10-20): `build.gradle:11-17,52,70` lists the nine modules, `androidModules` without servlet and SLF4J, `:NaruServe-servlet` main `api` `NaruServe-api` and the two `compileOnly` artifacts; the Maven Central metadata of `org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-servlet` lists `9.4.58.v20250814` as the last 9.4 release (Servlet 3.1, Java 8 runtime); the Gradle cache holds no `jetty-servlet` yet, so the first build resolves it from the network. Decision: Jetty 9.4 because it is the Servlet 3.1 line that runs on Java 8; Tomcat 8.5 is the alternative. Pitfall: Jetty 9.4 brings `javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` onto the test runtime class path only; `CON-BUILD-006 AC-5` is about the main `runtimeClasspath` and stays true. Pitfall: `CON-BUILD-009` forbids TinyHttpd components outside `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`, so the Servlet tests cannot reuse the TinyHttpd cross-adapter suite and compare with the in-memory adapter instead. Pitfall: Jetty 9.4 is end-of-life with known advisories; it is test-scope only and the vulnerability scan of FR-REL-002 covers the runtime dependencies of the published modules, not test scope. Rejected alternative: a `jakarta.servlet` module (Servlet 5+) in v1; Q-4 decided javax 3.1 only, reopen when a user needs Tomcat 10+.
acceptanceCriteria: The `compileClasspath` of `NaruServe-servlet` main holds `javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` and `javax.websocket-api:1.1` through `compileOnly` only, its main `runtimeClasspath` holds `NaruServe-api` and nothing else, and `BuildLayoutTest` (CON-BUILD-006 AC-1, AC-5) passes unchanged. `org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-servlet:9.4.58.v20250814` and `project(':NaruServe-gson')` are declared in `testImplementation` of `NaruServe-servlet` only, appear in no main configuration and on no other module's classpath, and no Jetty or Servlet class is on the classpath of `NaruServe-api` or any API 21 module; a build check lists the configurations that contain them. [D-362]

No Gradle module, dependency or class reference for `jakarta.servlet` exists, no API 21 module references `javax/servlet/` (the wave 1 class-reference check passes), and Gson 2.14.0 is the only Gson version on every module's classpath including the Servlet test classpath. [D-358; I-002; I-004; I-005]

The wave 8 change set contains no edit under `NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/spi` and removes or changes no public signature of `RestApp`, `Request`, `Response` or `HttpAdapter`, and the signature comparison test of IR-HTTP-007 AC-4 passes unchanged; the TinyHttpd checkout shows no modified file (CON-BUILD-010). [I-006; I-014; D-106]

title: docs/api/servlet.md records the Servlet adapter decisions without markers
requirement: The system shall rewrite `docs/api/servlet.md` so that it holds no (미확정) marker and records the registration, the class names and init-parameters, the lifecycle, the port, the path handling, multipart, WebSocket, SSE, stop, the ignored server options and the Gson lookup of the Servlet adapter, keeps the word `jakarta` in a sentence that says no `jakarta.servlet` module exists in v1, and shows Java and Kotlin examples with their Express counterpart sentence.
rationale: Covers D-363 (update `docs/api/servlet.md`), D-358 and every Servlet wave decision of loop W rounds 1 to 5, and the `docs/api` rule of CLAUDE.md that each API shows an Express counterpart and Java and Kotlin examples. Measured (2026-10-20): `docs/api/servlet.md` holds (미확정) markers on six lines (5, 11, 25, 26, 27, 29); `BuildLayoutTest` asserts that the file contains `jakarta` (OPS-BUILD-003 AC-5 "unchanged by wave 1"); the root `DocsExamplesCompileTest` compiles the Java blocks of `docs/api` and keeps a named skip list. Decision: the Express counterpart sentence reads that Express has no servlet container embedding and the closest equivalent is mounting the app on a host server. Pitfall: the sentence "jakarta.servlet(Servlet 5+)용은 별도 모듈로 나눌 예정입니다" must not stay as a promise; it becomes "v1에는 `jakarta.servlet` 모듈이 없습니다" (a post-v1 item with the Q-4 reason).
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/api/servlet.md` holds no (미확정) marker and contains `jakarta` in a sentence that states no `jakarta.servlet` module exists in v1 and that Servlet 5+ containers are not supported, which a docs test asserts together with the unchanged OPS-BUILD-003 AC-5 assertion. [D-363; D-358; D-380]

A registration section names `ServletConfigurer`, `NaruServeInitializer`, the init-parameters `naruserve.configurer` and `naruserve.urlPattern` with their defaults, the automatic discovery through the services file, `asyncSupported=true`, and shows a `web.xml` init-parameter example, a Java `ServletConfigurer` and a Kotlin one, with the Express counterpart sentence. [D-363; IR-SVL-001]

The comparison table and sections state: the container owns the port and `listen()` and `boundPort()` report `0` (take the port from the container); the container's destroy callback runs `shutdown`; the request path is the raw `getRequestURI()` minus the context path minus the url-pattern prefix, kept percent-encoded, an empty remainder is `/`, `;name=value` stays; multipart uses the core parser over the input stream, not the Servlet `Part` API; WebSocket is not supported and `app.ws` answers `501`; SSE runs under `AsyncContext` with an adapter-owned executor named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>`, `503` beyond `maxSseStreams`, `setTimeout(0)` and `asyncSupported`; the "cut at timeout" deviation; response header order is the container's; the `OPTIONS *` status observed; the Gson lookup by reflection and `Builder.jsonCodec`; and the thread total of the embedded engine does not apply. A docs test asserts a keyword of each. [D-363; FR-SVL-001; FR-SVL-002; FR-SVL-004; FR-SVL-005; FR-SVL-006; FR-SVL-007]

The ignored and applied `ServerOptions` lists of FR-SVL-008 AC-4 are present, and the Java examples of the file compile against the module through the root docs compile test or sit on its named skip list with an `absent type` reason, never with a silent skip. [D-363; I-009]

The Kotlin example of `servlet.md` is covered by the Kotlin examples test of FR-KT-004, and no line of `docs/api/sse.md` that wave 7 pinned changes: `sse.md` only gains a pointer sentence to the Servlet deviation. [D-349; I-008]
